beats.text: Every time your VLM agent controls a robot, it wastes massive compute by asking for a status update before every single micro-movement.
beats.visual_focus: A robotic arm stuttering as a text stream of redundant 'status?' tokens floods the screen.

visual_blueprint.title: THE BOTTLENECK
visual_blueprint.sub: Redundant token overhead in VLA policies

motif_params.title: THE BOTTLENECK
motif_params.sub: Redundant token overhead in VLA policies

beats.text: It is like a micromanager who demands a full report every time you move a single pixel, ignoring the actual goal at hand.
beats.visual_focus: A split screen: one side shows a smooth motion path, the other shows a jagged path interrupted by constant 'report' requests.

beats.text: PyRUA-Lean fixes this by shifting to interactive code execution, where the agent writes Python cells that handle local retries and conditional logic.
beats.visual_focus: A code block transforming from a list of prompts into a single, clean Python function with an 'if' statement.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This actually hit. I'm so tired of seeing 'AI agents' that just spam API calls until they hit a rate limit. The micromanager analogy in Beat 2 was solid—it didn't feel like some weird 'safe drawer' metaphor, it actually described the inefficiency of the current polling loop. I understood exactly why PyRUA-Lean is better: it moves the logic to the edge (the robot) instead of waiting for the model to re-process the whole context window for every tiny movement.
